newsitem.title: BOTSWANA: BIDDER SEES BOTSWANA CELLULAR NETWORK BY END OF YR.
newsitem.headline: BIDDER SEES BOTSWANA CELLULAR NETWORK BY END OF YR.

text.p: A Botswanan cellular telephone network should be up and running by the end of this year, a bidder for the licence said on Monday.

Botswana Vodacom Cellular (BVC), a partnership between Botswana Telecommunications Corporation (BTC) and South African cellular communications company Vodacom, will on Tuesday submit a bid for one of two licences expected to be granted by the end of September.

"I am 99.9 percent sure we will be granted a licence, I cannot imagine us not getting one...I expect to be using my cellphone in Botswana by Christmas." said Alan Knott-Craig, managing director of Vodacom.
No other companies have yet announced an intention to bid.

BTC chief executive Olebile Gaborone said BVC planned to invest 61 million pula in the network. The company would be owned 40 percent each by BTC and Vodacom and the remaining 20 percent offered to the public, possibly within 12 months.
